title: Site-stratified, patient-grouped splits + site-confounding audit
context: TCGA whole-slide images encode strong site/scanner signatures; a naive random split or patient-level-only split still leaks submitting site across the train/test boundary, inflating apparent generalization (Howard et al., 2021). This is the primary methodological problem the benchmark exists to fix. Leakage-safe, site-stratified splits are a primary artifact of the project — not an afterthought. The splits must be fixed, seeded, versioned, and published; a site-confounding audit must prove the splits do not trivially leak site. Domain-reviewer sign-off is required before the splits are published. This task is gated on M2 entry (domain reviewer secured by 2026-08-31). See PLAN.md (Splits + leakage control).
objective: Produce site-stratified, patient-grouped train/val/test splits for the tiled dataset: ensure no patient straddles the train/test boundary, and allocate submitting site so that site is not leaked across the split boundary. Fix, seed, version, and publish the split files. Conduct a site-confounding audit: train a probe to predict submitting site from model inputs and report recoverability (e.g. AUC) on the test split, with interpretation; surface, not hide, residual confounding. Record domain-reviewer sign-off on the splits.
acceptanceCriteria: Splits are site-stratified and patient-grouped: no patient straddles the train/test boundary, and submitting site is allocated so the split does not leak site across the train/test boundary.
A site-confounding audit trains a site-prediction probe on the test split and reports recoverability (e.g. AUC) with interpretation; residual confounding is surfaced and documented, not hidden.
Split files are fixed, seeded (seed value recorded), versioned, and published.
Domain-reviewer sign-off on the splits is recorded in the governance log.
Split files are committed as versioned artifacts (e.g. splits/v1/train.json, splits/v1/test.json) with the seed and split-ID recorded.
The site-confounding audit report is committed alongside the splits.
output: Published, versioned, seeded split files (train/val/test) with a site-confounding audit report, committed via PR, with domain-reviewer sign-off recorded.
